title: The Florida Keys
description:
The initial drive out to Bahia Honda Key, where my friend Canek and I camped, was easily the nicest drive I’ve done in the state of Florida. The scenery slowly transitions from the towns, like Homestead and Florida City, to endless swampland that grows more and more sparse, until finally you’re out over the turquoise blue water of the Strait of Florida. We found some of my dad’s old reggae CDs in the trunk and popped one in.

The sun was setting for what felt like an hour, and as it grew darker, the light from the Miami metro area faded away and more stars came out than I’ve ever seen on the mainland. The experience has an unsettling scale to it. Most of the islands along the drive are so small and flat that you can see their entire geography stretch out in front of you, as if on a map. But the other little islands, dotted out in a line like a breadcrumb trail, continue all the way to the horizon. It goes on forever—the drive from Miami to Key West takes about as long as the drive from Miami to Orlando—and so you become very acutely aware of both the size of your field of view and how tiny that is compared to the distance you’re going. Then you see your dad’s thumbprint on the next cd as you pop it in, and you remember you have Washington plates on your car, and you get a weird pit in your stomach. We checked in at Bahia Honda State Park, set up camp, and continued on for another hour until we made it into town.

“Where The Freaks At?” Key West stands as nature’s elegant response to one of mankind’s timeless questions. There is a huge colony of mutant six-toed cats established by Earnest Hemingway that roams the island to this day. Duvall Street reminded me of Bourbon Street except with more families and somehow more leather too.

Key West advertises itself as only 90 miles from Cuba. When it says that, it’s of course winking at you that it’s only 4 hours from Miami as well. It’s connected by the overseas highway, and this ease of access makes it feel like one of the less deserted paradises you’ve been to. The whole time we were out there, Canek couldn’t help but notice the small islands that the road hadn’t reached. On the second day, he was quick to ask our server, who had grown up in the Keys:

“Do you guys ever have parties out there?”

“Nah, some kids drowned and now the coast guard arrests anyone who tries that.”

“Got it.”

While we were out in Key West, we met this high end Miami strip club bottle girl named Tasha, along with her friend who was studying at a top 14 law school, and hung out with them on a park bench for a while. Tasha originally came up to us because her boss was “on her ass” for taking time off for a vacation, so she took a picture posing with Canek and I to use for promo for the club’s instagram. Tasha had met Drake for “like, the 3rd time” the week before, which didn’t seem like a big deal to her, and was making more money at the time than her friend could probably ever hope to, even at a white-shoe firm, which her friend didn't really seem to mind.

Tasha told us she was out in Key West to “reset” and get away from the fast life for a little. She had been in her line of work for a year now after doing real estate initially and felt in over her head sometimes. We found out that the two girls had flown in from Miami, rather than driving.

“If you guys can afford to fly, why didn’t you just go to the Bahamas, or Jamaica, or something?”

“Oh I go there for work! I just wanted something more real and grounded, you know?”

I thought about the 6-toed cats, and the bar on Duvall that becomes clothing optional at 11PM, and the young pretty Vietnamese lady who was being led around on a leash by an older white guy, and the vibrator vending machine.

Canek and I drove back to the campsite not long after. We didn’t say much. The next morning I woke up early to see the sunrise. Canek found me asleep on the beach 5 hours later and we packed up the tent before driving back up north. As we passed over one of the bridges between the breadcrumb islands, I imagined her flying above and wondered if the terrain Tasha saw stretching out below gave her the same sense of profundity as it gave me seeing it yawning out around us as we got to the next island. And then, of course, we got stuck in Miami traffic. 60 miles away from Miami.
